task_1.title: Deprecate scatter plot hue_style and rely on hue data type semantics
task_1.description: In xarray 2023.7.0, `hue_style` for 1D plots including scatter is deprecated because it no longer controls rendering. Scatter hue behavior is determined by the hue data itself: numeric values continue to use continuous color mapping, while non-numeric values behave categorically. Users should stop relying on `hue_style` to force discrete scatter coloring and instead control the displayed guide with legend or colorbar options.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that 1D and scatter plots no longer promise `hue_style` as a way to switch between discrete and continuous hue rendering, and ensure that users receive clear deprecation signaling while plots continue to behave consistently based on the hue variable type.

expectation.grounded: Calling `DataArray.plot.scatter` or other plot1d-based plotting APIs with `hue_style` should emit a `DeprecationWarning` indicating that `hue_style` is no longer used and will be removed later. For scatter plots, hue interpretation should follow the hue data type rather than the `hue_style` argument: numeric hue values remain continuous, string-like values are treated categorically, datetime hue values currently behave categorically, and timedelta hue values are accepted without requiring `hue_style`. Users can influence the displayed guide through `add_legend` and `add_colorbar`, and discrete treatment can be achieved by converting numeric hue values to strings.
expectation.conceptual: When users upgrade, scatter and similar 1D plots should no longer treat `hue_style` as an active control. Passing it should only warn that the option is deprecated. Plot coloring should instead follow the natural kind of data supplied for hue, and users should use legend or colorbar controls, or categorical hue values, to get the presentation they want.

constraints.grounded: Existing plot1d and scatter calls must remain executable even when `hue_style` is provided, but they must warn instead of changing rendering. Numeric hue inputs must continue to produce mappable continuous coloring. Faceted scatter plots must still produce valid matplotlib scatter mappables for numeric, datetime, and string hue inputs. Datetime hue support must not fail even though it is currently treated as categorical rather than numeric.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade must preserve plot operability and avoid breaking common scatter workflows, while making it explicit that `hue_style` no longer changes results. Different hue value kinds should continue to render consistently across regular and faceted plots, without introducing crashes for date-like inputs.

behavior: Using `hue_style` with plot1d-based plots now raises a `DeprecationWarning` instead of affecting plot appearance.
Scatter plot hue rendering is determined by the hue data type rather than an explicit discrete or continuous style switch.
Numeric hue values continue to use continuous color mapping.
String or other non-numeric categorical hue values render categorically.
Datetime hue values are accepted and currently render categorically.
Timedelta hue values are accepted without relying on `hue_style`.
Legend and colorbar display remain user-controlled through the existing plot guide options.
acceptance_criteria: When a user passes `hue_style` to a scatter or other plot1d-based plotting call, the plot should still run and should emit a `DeprecationWarning`.
When a user plots scatter data with a numeric hue variable, the result should use continuous color semantics regardless of any `hue_style` value.
When a user plots scatter data with categorical string hue values, the result should use categorical hue semantics without requiring `hue_style`.
When a user plots scatter data with datetime hue values, the plotting call should succeed and treat the hue categorically under the current behavior.
When a user plots scatter data with timedelta hue values, the plotting call should succeed without needing `hue_style`.
When a user creates faceted scatter plots with numeric, datetime, or string hue values, the plots should still produce valid scatter mappables and remain renderable.

When a user wants a discrete presentation for numeric hue values, the supported contract should be to supply categorical-like hue values and use legend or colorbar controls rather than depending on `hue_style`.

task_2.title: Reject forward slashes in HDF5-backed NetCDF variable and dimension names
task_2.description: The upgrade adds early validation for dataset variable names and dimension names when writing through HDF5-based NetCDF engines. Instead of crashing later during write or readback, xarray now fails fast with a clear ValueError when a name contains a forward slash, because that character conflicts with HDF5 hierarchy semantics.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that exporting datasets with HDF5-based NetCDF engines does not crash unexpectedly when variable or dimension names contain '/'. Ensure invalid names are rejected up front with a clear validation error.

expectation.grounded: When Dataset.to_netcdf uses the HDF5-based engines backed by netcdf4 or h5netcdf, xarray should validate variable names and dimension names before creating dimensions or variables. If any such name contains a forward slash, the operation should raise ValueError rather than proceeding to backend write logic or failing later during round-trip access.
expectation.conceptual: Writing a dataset to HDF5-backed NetCDF output should fail fast for names that are not representable in that storage model. Names containing '/' should be treated as invalid and reported immediately with a normal validation error.

constraints.grounded: The validation applies specifically to variable and dimension names used by the HDF5-based NetCDF backends. Valid names without forward slashes must continue to write successfully, including normal round-trip behavior. The observable failure mode for invalid names should be ValueError, not a backend lookup failure or late crash.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must only block truly unsupported names and must not regress successful exports for otherwise valid datasets. The user-facing behavior should be deterministic and consistent across supported HDF5-backed engines.

behavior: Datasets with a variable name containing '/' are rejected when written with HDF5-based NetCDF engines.
Datasets with a dimension name containing '/' are rejected when written with HDF5-based NetCDF engines.
The rejection occurs before the backend completes the write or attempts round-trip variable access.
The failure is surfaced as ValueError instead of an indirect backend error such as a missing variable lookup.
acceptance_criteria: When a dataset contains a variable name with '/', writing it with an HDF5-based NetCDF engine should raise ValueError.
When a dataset contains a dimension name with '/', writing it with an HDF5-based NetCDF engine should raise ValueError.
When dataset variable and dimension names do not contain '/', writing with the same engines should continue to succeed.
When invalid names are provided, the error should occur during the write attempt itself rather than after a partially completed write or round-trip read.

task_3.title: Expand xarray Dataset API docstrings with executable examples
task_3.description: The 2023.7.0 update expands xarray Dataset API documentation by adding worked examples and related documentation links for common Dataset methods. The change improves discoverability and clarifies expected usage and results for coordinate conversion, row selection helpers, missing-value handling, and equality or attribute-oriented Dataset operations without changing runtime semantics.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that xarray 2023.7.0 provides clearer, user-facing documentation for common `Dataset` operations by including concrete examples and related references, so users can understand expected inputs, outputs, and edge-case behavior without relying on source inspection.

expectation.grounded: The release note and diff together indicate that xarray should expose expanded docstrings for public `Dataset` APIs, including examples for methods such as `Dataset.assign_attrs()`, `Dataset.broadcast_equals()`, `Dataset.equals()`, `Dataset.identical()`, `Dataset.expand_dims()`, `Dataset.drop_vars()`, `Dataset.set_coords()`, `Dataset.reset_coords()`, `Dataset.head()`, `Dataset.tail()`, `Dataset.dropna()`, `Dataset.ffill()`, and `Dataset.bfill()`. These docstrings should demonstrate observable behavior such as coordinate-to-variable conversion, variable-to-coordinate conversion, dimensional slicing via integer or mapping inputs, dropping labels based on missing-data rules, and bounded forward or backward filling. Related methods should be cross-referenced where applicable.
expectation.conceptual: Users upgrading to 2023.7.0 should find that major `Dataset` APIs are better documented with practical examples that show what the operation returns and how option values affect results. The library should be easier to learn and verify through documentation alone, while preserving the same public behavior.

constraints.grounded: This upgrade should not alter the runtime contract of the documented `Dataset` methods. Existing return types, argument forms, and observable behaviors for equality checks, attribute assignment, dimension expansion, coordinate resets, variable drops, head or tail selection, NA filtering, and forward or backward fill must remain unchanged; the update is limited to documentation clarity and examples.
constraints.conceptual: The improvement must be non-breaking. It should add clarity and examples without changing how these APIs behave in user code or requiring code changes from existing consumers.

behavior: `Dataset` documentation now includes more concrete examples for common data-manipulation methods.
Examples show that coordinate-related APIs convert variables and coordinates while preserving Dataset structure according to the documented operation.
Examples for `head()` and `tail()` show selection by a scalar count and by per-dimension mapping input.
Examples for `dropna()` show different observable outcomes for `how="any"`, `how="all"`, and `thresh`.
Examples for `ffill()` and `bfill()` show propagation along a named dimension and how `limit` bounds consecutive fill operations.
Related `Dataset` methods are linked in documentation where that relationship helps users navigate equivalent or inverse operations.
acceptance_criteria: When a user reads the 2023.7.0 documentation for the affected public `Dataset` methods, it should include at least one practical example of calling the method and observing the returned Dataset or boolean result.
When a user consults documentation for coordinate conversion APIs, it should clearly illustrate the effect of converting data variables to coordinates and coordinates to data variables.
When a user consults documentation for `head()` or `tail()`, it should show both count-based and dimension-mapping-based selection behavior.
When a user consults documentation for `dropna()`, it should distinguish the effects of dropping labels for any missing values, all missing values, and threshold-based filtering.
When a user consults documentation for `ffill()` or `bfill()`, it should show both unrestricted filling and filling constrained by `limit`.
When existing user code calls the documented methods after upgrading to 2023.7.0, it should continue to behave the same as before because the change is documentation-only.

task_4.title: Document alternative chunked array backends
task_4.description: Version 2023.7.0 adds user-facing guidance for using chunked numpy-like arrays as alternatives to dask arrays and clarifies the public chunk manager interface that such backends are expected to implement. The update formalizes the observable contract around chunk manager registration, chunk detection, chunk normalization, array wrapping, computation, generalized ufunc support, block operations, chunk unification, and storage.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that users and backend authors can understand and rely on xarray's supported contract for wrapping chunked numpy-like arrays as alternatives to dask arrays, including how such arrays are recognized, chunked, computed, transformed, and written through the chunk manager interface.

expectation.grounded: xarray should document `ChunkManagerEntrypoint` as the public interface for parallel or chunked array backends registered through the `chunkmanagers` entry point. The documented contract should make clear that `list_chunkmanagers()` exposes registered chunk manager entrypoint objects, that `array_cls` is used for runtime instance checks, and that backends are expected to provide observable behaviors for `is_chunked_array`, `chunks`, `normalize_chunks`, `from_array`, `compute`, `apply_gufunc`, `map_blocks`, `unify_chunks`, and `store`, with optional methods such as `rechunk`, `reduction`, `blockwise`, and `array_api` enabling additional xarray functionality or otherwise raising `NotImplementedError` when unavailable.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to use xarray with supported chunked array libraries other than dask, and backend authors should have a clear, stable description of the behavior their integration must expose so xarray can detect arrays, preserve chunk information, execute computations, apply array operations, and write results consistently.

constraints.grounded: The update should not change core runtime semantics for existing chunked backends. Documented behavior must preserve that chunk managers operate on numpy-like chunked arrays, return explicit normalized chunk structures where required, compute chunked inputs into eager arrays while allowing non-chunked inputs to pass through unchanged, and only support optional xarray features when the corresponding non-abstract interface is implemented.
constraints.conceptual: Existing integrations should continue to behave as before, while the documented contract should define clear boundaries for what every backend must support versus what is optional. Alternative chunked array support should remain compatible with normal xarray computation and I/O expectations without imposing new behavior on users who stay on existing backends.

behavior: xarray documents support for wrapping chunked numpy-like arrays as alternatives to dask arrays.
Registered chunk managers are presented as backend interface objects discoverable through the chunk manager registry.
Chunked array detection is defined in terms of the backend's declared array class and backend-specific `is_chunked_array` behavior.
Chunk structure exposure and chunk normalization are part of the required backend contract for chunk-aware operations such as dataset opening and chunk inspection.
Creating a chunked array from a non-chunked numpy-like source and rechunking an already chunked array are documented as distinct backend responsibilities.
Computing chunked arrays is defined to return eager numpy results while tolerating non-chunked arguments in the same call.
Support for generalized ufunc application, block mapping, chunk unification, and chunk-aware storage is documented as part of the backend interoperability surface.
Some advanced xarray features depend on optional backend methods and may be unavailable when those methods are not implemented.
acceptance_criteria: When a user consults the 2023.7.0 documentation for chunked arrays, it should describe how to use chunked numpy-like arrays as alternatives to dask arrays.

When a backend author implements and registers a `ChunkManagerEntrypoint`, the documented contract should identify which methods are mandatory and which methods only enable additional xarray functionality.
When xarray encounters an object belonging to a registered backend's chunked array type, the documented behavior should explain how that object is recognized as chunked.
When chunk-aware operations inspect or derive chunking, the documented behavior should require explicit normalized chunk information from the backend.
When xarray computes one or more backend-managed chunked arrays, the documented behavior should state that eager numpy results are returned and unrelated non-chunked objects are preserved.

When users rely on operations such as generalized ufunc application, block mapping, chunk unification, or backend-backed writes, the documented interface should make clear that backend support for these operations is part of interoperability with xarray.

When an optional chunk manager capability is not implemented, the documented contract should make clear that only the related subset of xarray functionality is unavailable rather than implying full backend incompatibility.

task_5.title: Clarify chunked duck-array integration contracts
task_5.description: The 2023.7.0 update expands user-facing documentation for wrapping numpy-like duck arrays and, in particular, clarifies the public integration contract for chunked array backends via xarray's chunk manager entrypoints. The release makes the expected capabilities, supported operations, and fallback behavior explicit for backend authors and advanced users adopting non-dask chunked arrays such as cubed-backed arrays.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading users and chunked duck-array backend authors can rely on clearly documented support expectations for wrapping numpy-like arrays and integrating chunked array frameworks with xarray, including which `ChunkManagerEntrypoint` methods are required, which xarray operations depend on them, and what behavior is expected when optional capabilities are not implemented.

expectation.grounded: The documentation for `xarray.core.parallelcompat.ChunkManagerEntrypoint` and related chunk-manager APIs should describe `list_chunkmanagers`, runtime type detection via `array_cls` and `is_chunked_array`, and the observable contracts for `chunks`, `normalize_chunks`, `from_array`, `rechunk`, `compute`, `array_api`, `reduction`, `apply_gufunc`, `map_blocks`, `blockwise`, `unify_chunks`, and `store`. It should state that subclasses must implement abstract methods, that non-abstract methods only enable a subset of xarray functionality, and that unsupported optional operations may raise `NotImplementedError` when invoked.
expectation.conceptual: Users should have a clear description of how xarray works with chunked duck arrays, what capabilities a backend must provide to participate in core operations, and which advanced behaviors are optional and may be unavailable unless the backend implements them. The upgrade should make support boundaries and expected outcomes understandable without changing existing runtime semantics.

constraints.grounded: Do not change public behavior for existing chunk-manager integrations solely as part of this update. Preserve the documented distinction between required abstract methods and optional non-abstract methods, keep runtime instance checking based on the backend's declared array type, and avoid implying support for operations such as `apply_ufunc`, `unify_chunks`, backend writes, or chunked reductions unless the corresponding `ChunkManagerEntrypoint` capability is implemented.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should improve clarity without introducing new behavioral guarantees beyond what supported backends already provide. Backends that do not implement optional features should continue to fail in a clear, expected way rather than appearing fully supported.

behavior: Chunk-manager discovery is described as returning registered `ChunkManagerEntrypoint` implementations keyed by their registration names.
Chunked-array detection is documented as runtime instance checking against the backend-declared array class, with `is_chunked_array` available for that purpose.
Creating, normalizing, and rechunking chunked arrays are documented as distinct backend responsibilities used by `.chunk()` and `open_dataset()` workflows.
Computing chunked arrays is documented as supporting one or more inputs and passing through non-chunked objects unchanged while returning computed in-memory results for chunked inputs.
Most xarray computations are documented as depending on backend support for generalized ufunc application via `apply_gufunc`.

Elementwise block mapping, generalized blockwise operations, chunk unification, reductions, and backend storage are documented as separate optional backend capabilities tied to specific xarray operations.
Optional chunk-manager methods are documented as enabling subsets of functionality and may raise `NotImplementedError` when unsupported features are called.
Duck-array guidance is expanded to cover non-dask chunked backends, including cross-references for cubed as an example ecosystem integration.
acceptance_criteria: When a developer reads the upgraded guidance for wrapping chunked duck arrays, it should clearly distinguish required `ChunkManagerEntrypoint` methods from optional ones.

When a backend author checks how xarray identifies chunked arrays, the documentation should state that runtime detection is based on the backend's declared array class and `is_chunked_array` behavior.

When a user or integrator looks up `.chunk()` or `open_dataset()` interactions with non-dask chunked arrays, the documentation should explain which backend hooks govern chunk normalization, array creation, and rechunking.
When a developer wants to support general xarray computation on a custom chunked backend, the documentation should indicate that `apply_gufunc` support is needed for most xarray operations.

When optional operations such as chunk unification, blockwise execution, reductions, or storage are not implemented by a backend, the documented expectation should be that those features are unavailable and may raise `NotImplementedError` if used.
When comparing 2023.6.0 to 2023.7.0, users should observe a documentation and guidance improvement rather than a required migration or changed runtime API behavior.

task_6.title: Add usage examples for core Dataset selection and aggregation APIs
task_6.description: The 2023.7.0 update improves xarray's user-facing documentation by adding concrete examples to Dataset.isel(), Dataset.reduce(), Dataset.argmin(), and Dataset.argmax(). The new material clarifies how these APIs behave with scalar indexing, slices, DataArray indexers, reductions over dimensions, and index-producing aggregation results, making expected outputs easier to understand without changing runtime behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the upgrade documents how key Dataset selection and aggregation methods are expected to behave in common usage, including positional indexing, reductions across dimensions, and interpreting argmin/argmax results.

expectation.grounded: The public docstrings for xarray.Dataset.isel, xarray.Dataset.reduce, xarray.Dataset.argmin, and xarray.Dataset.argmax should include runnable examples that demonstrate observable results. Dataset.isel should show scalar selection, slice-based selection, and selection with a DataArray indexer. Dataset.reduce should show reduction with a user-supplied function such as numpy.percentile over a named dimension and return a Dataset with the reduced dimension removed. Dataset.argmin and Dataset.argmax should show that they return a Dataset of positional indices per variable for the requested dimension, and that those indices can be used with Dataset coordinates via isel to recover the labels corresponding to minima or maxima. Dataset.argmin documentation should also reference Dataset.idxmin as a related label-oriented API.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to read the API documentation and immediately understand, from concrete examples, what these Dataset methods return and how to use the results. The docs should make it clear how positional indexing works, how reducing over a dimension changes the shape of the result, and how argmin or argmax outputs can be used to identify where extrema occur.

constraints.grounded: This update should not change the runtime behavior, signatures, return types, or error behavior of Dataset.isel, Dataset.reduce, Dataset.argmin, or Dataset.argmax. The added examples must stay aligned with the documented public API and produce observable outputs consistent with existing semantics for positional selection, dimension reduction, and index-returning extrema operations.
constraints.conceptual: The change is documentation-only. It must improve clarity without altering how the library behaves or introducing contradictions between examples and actual API behavior.

behavior: Dataset.isel documentation now illustrates selecting a single element by integer positions, subsetting with slices, and indexing with a DataArray-based positional indexer.
Dataset.reduce documentation now illustrates applying a reduction function across a named dimension and returning a Dataset whose reduced dimension is removed from the result.

Dataset.argmin documentation now illustrates that the method returns per-variable positional indices for minima along the requested dimension and that those indices can be used with isel on coordinates to recover corresponding labels.
Dataset.argmax documentation now illustrates that the method returns per-variable positional indices for maxima along the requested dimension.
Dataset.argmin documentation now points users to Dataset.idxmin as a related API for label-oriented minimum lookup.
acceptance_criteria: When reading the Dataset.isel documentation, users should find examples covering integer indexing, slice indexing, and DataArray-based positional indexing, each with the resulting Dataset shape and coordinates made explicit.

When reading the Dataset.reduce documentation, users should find an example of reducing over a named dimension with a supplied function and see that the output Dataset no longer includes the reduced dimension.

When reading the Dataset.argmin documentation, users should find an example showing that the returned object contains positional indices for each variable and that those indices can be used to obtain the coordinate labels where minima occur.
When reading the Dataset.argmax documentation, users should find an example showing that the returned object contains positional indices for each variable along the specified dimension.

When comparing behavior before and after the upgrade, Dataset.isel, Dataset.reduce, Dataset.argmin, and Dataset.argmax should behave the same at runtime; only the documentation should become more explicit and instructive.

task_7.title: Broaden flox-backed grouped reductions to supported chunked arrays
task_7.description: The upgrade broadens xarray's flox-backed aggregation path so grouped reductions are no longer limited to dask-backed data. DataArray and Dataset operations that rely on flox may now accept other supported chunked array implementations, improving compatibility for chunked non-dask arrays while preserving existing behavior for NumPy and dask inputs.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that flox-backed grouped reduction operations accept supported chunked non-dask arrays in addition to NumPy and dask-backed data, without changing the observable behavior of existing supported inputs.

expectation.grounded: When flox is available and the `use_flox` option is enabled, xarray should allow DataArray and Dataset groupby and resample aggregation methods to proceed when their variables are backed by NumPy arrays or by chunked array types recognized by xarray, rather than restricting the flox path to dask arrays only. This applies to observable aggregation entry points such as `count`, `all`, `any`, `max`, `min`, `mean`, `prod`, `sum`, `std`, and `var`.
expectation.conceptual: Grouped and resampled reductions should work with supported chunked array backends, not just dask, whenever the optimized flox execution path is enabled. Users should be able to use the same public aggregation APIs and get normal reduction behavior for eligible chunked arrays.

constraints.grounded: Existing acceptance of NumPy-backed and dask-backed inputs must remain unchanged. The flox path should still depend on flox availability and the `use_flox` option being enabled. Inputs containing unsupported non-NumPy, non-chunked data should not be newly treated as eligible for the flox-backed path solely because of this change.
constraints.conceptual: The change should expand backend compatibility without altering how existing supported arrays behave or bypassing the normal conditions for optimized grouped reductions. Unsupported data types should not silently gain support unless they meet the same chunked-array eligibility rules.

behavior: Flox-backed grouped reductions now consider xarray-supported chunked array backends eligible, instead of only dask-backed arrays.
The expanded eligibility applies to both DataArray and Dataset aggregation APIs.
The same eligibility broadening is used across common grouped reduction methods, including count, logical reductions, numeric reductions, and variance-related reductions.
When flox is unavailable or disabled, the change does not require a different execution path or user-facing API.
NumPy-backed and dask-backed inputs continue to behave as supported inputs for flox-backed grouped reductions.
acceptance_criteria: When a DataArray or Dataset is backed by a supported chunked non-dask array type and flox is available with `use_flox` enabled, invoking a supported groupby reduction should be accepted by xarray instead of being rejected solely because the backend is not dask.

When a DataArray or Dataset is backed by a supported chunked non-dask array type and flox is available with `use_flox` enabled, invoking a supported resample reduction should be accepted under the same eligibility rules.
When a DataArray or Dataset is backed by NumPy arrays, supported grouped reductions should continue to work as before.
When a DataArray or Dataset is backed by dask arrays, supported grouped reductions should continue to work as before.
When flox is unavailable or `use_flox` is disabled, the presence of a supported chunked non-dask backend should not by itself imply a changed API contract for grouped reductions.
When object variables are not NumPy-backed and are not recognized as supported chunked arrays, they should not newly qualify for flox-backed grouped reduction handling because of this upgrade.
